turns.text: Behind the technical name Fully Convolutional Networks, what intuitive problem were researchers confronting?

Classification CNNs produced one label for an image, while semantic segmentation required a label at every pixel. Fully Convolutional Networks showed how classification networks could be converted into end-to-end dense predictors.
That sounds like a promising direction. What mechanism actually makes it work?

Fully connected layers are replaced by convolutions so arbitrary-size images produce spatial score maps. Learned upsampling and skip connections combine coarse semantic information with finer spatial detail.
Why did the idea outlive one paper or experiment? What did later researchers actually inherit?

Experts generally regard FCN as the template that established modern end-to-end semantic segmentation. Its conversion, upsampling, and skip-fusion ideas became foundations for U-Net, DeepLab, and many dense prediction systems.
Fully Convolutional Networks mattered not only as a result, but as a method that later researchers could test, adapt, and extend.
